question: If PQRS is a rhombus such that ∠PRQ = 40°, then ∠PSQ is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **rhombus**, the diagonals are **perpendicular** to each other and **bisect** the interior angles.

∠PRQ = 40° ⇒ ∠QRS = 2 × 40° = 80°.

Adjacent angles of a rhombus are **supplementary**: ∠PQR = 180° − 80° = 100°.

Since the diagonal **SQ bisects ∠PSR** and triangles are congruent, ∠PSQ = (180° − ∠PQR) ÷ 2 = 100° ÷ 2 = 50°.

Alternatively, in right triangle **SMR** (where M is the intersection), ∠PSQ = 90° − ∠PRQ = 90° − 40° = 50°.

**∴ The correct answer is 50°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **PQRS** is a **rhombus** and ∠PRQ = 40°.

**Formula Used:** Diagonals of a rhombus **bisect each other at 90°** and bisect the **vertex angles**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6028934451a527f243c326fe10ff64c323ca9b1a293124e79781060a06db1f57.png] 

⇒ In rhombus **PQRS**, let diagonals **PR** and **SQ** intersect at **M**.

⇒ ∠PMR = 90° (Diagonals are perpendicular).

⇒ In ΔSMR, ∠SMR = 90°.

⇒ Since **PQ || SR** (opposite sides are parallel), ∠PRQ = ∠SPR = 40° (Alternate interior angles).

⇒ In ΔPMS, ∠PMS = 90° and ∠SPR = 40°.

⇒ ∠PSQ = 180° − (∠PMS + ∠SPR)

⇒ ∠PSQ = 180° − (90° + 40°)

⇒ ∠PSQ = 180° − 130° = 50°.

**∴ The correct answer is 50°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

All sides are equal, and diagonals bisect each other at right angles (90°).

Angle Bisector Property

Each diagonal of a rhombus bisects the interior angles of the vertices it joins.

Adjacent Angles

The sum of any two adjacent angles in a rhombus is 180° (supplementary).</p
